updates.name: Janet A. Nye
updates.bio: Professor at UNC Chapel Hill and Director of its Institute of Marine Sciences, specializing in fisheries oceanography, ecology and management. The Nye Lab applies mathematical and statistical tools to examine how environmental variability and human-driven climate change alter fish populations and marine ecosystems, including where fish live, how productive their stocks are, and predator-prey dynamics.
updates.research_interests: fisheries oceanography; climate and environmental variability effects on fish populations; fish spatial distribution and productivity; effects of temperature, circulation and fishing; predator-prey interactions; emergent ecosystem properties
updates.current_title: Professor; Director, Institute of Marine Sciences
updates.current_affiliation: Earth, Marine and Environmental Sciences / Institute of Marine Sciences, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
updates.evidence: Janet Nye Professor Director of the Institute of Marine Sciences
updates.notes: Old homepage https://ims.unc.edu/people/jnye/ 301s to https://emes.unc.edu/ims/people/jnye/ which is 404; replaced with the EMES profile (200), which links the Nye Lab site https://nye.unc.edu/ and Google Scholar user=t--shiUAAAAJ. Lake title 'Associate Professor' is out of date.

updates.name: Nicole Cabana
updates.bio: Acting Director of NOAA's Northeast Fisheries Science Center in Woods Hole. She came to the center in 2018 as a NOAA Corps officer serving as Chief of Staff and became its civilian Deputy Director in 2020, after two decades in the Corps spent on ship operations, diving and research flights. Trained in marine biology and engineering; also a licensed pilot.
updates.current_title: Acting Director, Northeast Fisheries Science Center
updates.current_affiliation: NOAA Fisheries, Northeast Fisheries Science Center
updates.evidence: Nicole Cabana is the Acting Director at the Northeast Fisheries Science Center (NEFSC) in Woods Hole, MA.
updates.notes: Page uses she/her for this person. Lake role is deputy-director; the page and https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/about/northeast-fisheries-science-center now list her as Acting Director (Paula Fratantoni, Ph.D. listed as Acting NEFSC Deputy Director) - a research batch should update the NEFSC director/deputy rows. updates.name: Jerome Fiechter
updates.bio: Associate Professor in the Ocean Sciences Department and Institute of Marine Sciences at UC Santa Cruz, working across physical and biological oceanography with numerical models of coastal marine ecosystem dynamics. Holds mechanical engineering degrees from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (BS) and Georgia Tech (MS) and a doctorate in applied marine physics from the University of Miami.
updates.research_interests: physical oceanography; biological oceanography; coastal marine ecosystem dynamics; numerical and computational modeling; coastal science
updates.current_affiliation: Ocean Sciences Department and Institute of Marine Sciences, University of California Santa Cruz

updates.name: Adrienne Canino
updates.bio: Data librarian at Axiom Data Science whose career runs from environmental conservation to research data services, including data literacy initiatives, digital archiving and coordinating a youth conservation corps. Holds a 2014 master's in environmental studies from SUNY ESF and a 2018 MLIS from Syracuse University.

The announcement cites a background spanning marine research and ocean policy.

updates.name: Timothy K. Kratz
updates.bio: Director of UW-Madison's Trout Lake Station, named in a 2010 College of Letters & Science notice as taking a one-to-two-year post as a rotating program officer in the National Science Foundation's Ecosystems Science Cluster, while staying involved remotely in LTER research, GLEON (the Global Lake Ecological Observatory Network) and a mixing experiment on Crystal Lake.
updates.research_interests: long-term regional ecology of lakes; interactions between people and lakes; wetland ecology; Little Rock Lake research
updates.evidence: Tim Kratz, Director of the Trout Lake Station, has accepted a position as a rotating Program Officer
updates.notes: Bio source is a UW-Madison College of Letters & Science news item dated October 20, 2010 (200); bio is date-bound to it. Research interests from the Wisconsin Public Radio contributor profile https://wpr.org/person/tim-kratz (200), which calls him director of the UW Trout Lake Station, part of the Center for Limnology, and says he has worked on Little Rock Lake since 1983; WXPR contributor profile https://www.wxpr.org/people/tim-kratz (200) also credits him as a GLEON founder. Neither is used as homepage. Existing homepage https://limnology.wisc.edu/staff/kratz-timothy/ returns 404. No fetched page states he is emeritus or retired, so status and current title are left null (the lake's 'emeritus' value is unsourced). No ORCID linked on any fetched page.
